title: 梦游天姥吟留别
title_en: A Dream Journey to Mount Tianmu: A Farewell Song
author: 李白

form.en: old-style song with lines of mixed length

text_note.zh: 这里用的是现在课本里的通行文字。古籍收录的文字有几处不同：“云霞明灭”一作“云霓明灭”；“洞天石扉”一作“洞天石扇”；“别君去兮何时还”一作“别君去时何时还”。“睹”“猿”“恍”在古籍里写作“覩”“猨”“怳”。这首诗又题作《梦游天姥山别东鲁诸公》。
text_note.en: This is the text taught in schools today. Old collections differ in a few places. Yún xiá (“rosy clouds”) appears as yún ní (“rainbow clouds”). Shí fēi (“stone door”) appears as shí shàn (“stone door leaf”). Bié jūn qù xī (“I leave you, oh”) appears as bié jūn qù shí (“when I leave you”). A few characters are written in older forms. The poem is also titled “Dreaming of Mount Tianmu, a Farewell to Friends in Eastern Lu”.

readings.zh: 山名“天姥”中读 mǔ，不读 lǎo。
readings.en: In the mountain name Tianmu it is read mǔ, not lǎo.

readings.zh: 山名“天台”中读 tāi，不读 tái。
readings.en: In the mountain name Tiantai it is read tāi, not tái.
Meaning to fall over, read dǎo.

readings.zh: 地名“剡溪”中读 shàn，不读 yǎn。
readings.en: In the place name Shanxi it is read shàn, not yǎn.
Meaning to stay overnight, read sù.

readings.zh: 形容雷声，读 yǐn，不读 yīn 或 yān。
readings.en: Describing the rumble of thunder, read yǐn, not yīn or yān.
Meaning to wake up, read jué, not jiào.
Meaning to come back, read huán.

glosses.zh: 海客：在海上航行的人，见过很多远方的事。
glosses.en: hǎi kè: seafarers, people who sail the sea and have heard of faraway things.

glosses.zh: 瀛洲：传说中东海里的一座仙山，和蓬莱、方丈合称三神山。
glosses.en: yíng zhōu: a magic island of immortals said to lie in the Eastern Sea, one of the Three Divine Mountains with Penglai and Fangzhang.

glosses.zh: 烟涛：像烟雾一样迷蒙的波涛。
glosses.en: yān tāo: misty, smoke-like waves.

glosses.zh: 微茫：模模糊糊，看不清楚。
glosses.en: wēi máng: dim and blurry.

glosses.zh: 信难求：实在难以找到。信，确实。
glosses.en: xìn nán qiú: truly hard to find. Xìn means truly.

glosses.zh: 越人：越地的人。越地就是今天的浙江一带。
glosses.en: yuè rén: people of Yue, the region of today's Zhejiang.

glosses.zh: 语：说起。
glosses.en: yǔ: to talk about.

glosses.zh: 天姥：天姥山，在今浙江新昌县东。相传登山的人能听到仙女（天姥）唱歌，所以叫这个名字。姥，读 mǔ。
glosses.en: tiān mǔ: Mount Tianmu, east of today's Xinchang County in Zhejiang. Legend says climbers could hear a heavenly old woman singing, hence the name.

glosses.zh: 明灭：一会儿亮，一会儿暗。
glosses.en: míng miè: now bright, now dim.

glosses.zh: 或可睹：也许能看到。或，也许；睹，看见。
glosses.en: huò kě dǔ: may perhaps be seen. Huò means perhaps; dǔ means to see.

glosses.zh: 连天：和天连在一起，形容极高。
glosses.en: lián tiān: joined to the sky, meaning extremely high.

glosses.zh: 向天横：向天边伸展开去，挡住了天空。横，横着伸展。
glosses.en: xiàng tiān héng: stretching across the sky. Héng means to lie across.

glosses.zh: 势拔五岳：山势超过了五岳。拔，超出；五岳，泰山、华山、衡山、恒山、嵩山五座名山。
glosses.en: shì bá wǔ yuè: its height rises above the Five Great Mountains. Bá means to rise above; the Five Great Mountains are Tai, Hua, Heng (in Hunan), Heng (in Shanxi) and Song.

glosses.zh: 掩：遮盖，压倒。
glosses.en: yǎn: to overshadow.

glosses.zh: 赤城：赤城山，在今浙江天台县北，山上的土石是红色的。
glosses.en: chì chéng: Mount Chicheng, north of today's Tiantai County in Zhejiang, known for its red rocks.

glosses.zh: 天台：天台山，在今浙江天台县北。这里“台”读 tāi。
glosses.en: tiān tāi: Mount Tiantai, north of today's Tiantai County in Zhejiang.

glosses.zh: 四万八千丈：夸张的说法，形容非常高。
glosses.en: sì wàn bā qiān zhàng: an exaggeration, meaning very, very high.

glosses.zh: 对此欲倒东南倾：对着天姥山，好像要拜倒在它脚下，向东南方向倾斜。此，指天姥山。
glosses.en: duì cǐ yù dǎo dōng nán qīng: facing Mount Tianmu, it seems ready to bow down and lean away to the southeast. Cǐ refers to Mount Tianmu.

glosses.zh: 因之：根据越人说的话。因，依据；之，指越人的话。
glosses.en: yīn zhī: because of what the people of Yue said. Yīn means based on; zhī refers to their words.

glosses.zh: 梦吴越：在梦里游吴越一带。吴越，今江苏、浙江一带。
glosses.en: mèng wú yuè: to travel in a dream to Wu and Yue, around today's Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

glosses.zh: 度：越过。
glosses.en: dù: to cross.

glosses.zh: 镜湖：又叫鉴湖，在今浙江绍兴南。湖水像镜子一样平。
glosses.en: jìng hú: Mirror Lake, also called Jian Lake, south of today's Shaoxing in Zhejiang. Its water is as smooth as a mirror.

glosses.zh: 剡溪：水名，在今浙江嵊州南。剡，读 shàn。
glosses.en: shàn xī: the Shan Stream, south of today's Shengzhou in Zhejiang.

glosses.zh: 谢公：南朝诗人谢灵运。他游天姥山时，曾在剡溪住过。
glosses.en: xiè gōng: Xie Lingyun, a poet of the Southern Dynasties. When he visited Mount Tianmu, he stayed by the Shan Stream.

glosses.zh: 宿处：住过的地方。
glosses.en: sù chù: the place where he stayed.

glosses.zh: 渌水：清澈的水。
glosses.en: lù shuǐ: clear water.

glosses.zh: 荡漾：水波一起一伏地晃动。
glosses.en: dàng yàng: rippling gently.

glosses.zh: 清猿啼：猿猴发出清亮的叫声。
glosses.en: qīng yuán tí: apes calling in clear voices.

glosses.zh: 著：穿。这里读 zhuó。
glosses.en: zhuó: to wear.

glosses.zh: 谢公屐：谢灵运特制的一种登山木鞋，鞋底装着可以拆下的齿。上山时去掉前齿，下山时去掉后齿，走起来更稳。
glosses.en: xiè gōng jī: Xie Lingyun's special wooden hiking shoes. The soles had removable spikes: he took off the front ones going uphill and the back ones going downhill, so he walked steadily.

glosses.zh: 青云梯：高入云霄的石阶山路。
glosses.en: qīng yún tī: stone steps climbing high into the clouds.

glosses.zh: 半壁：半山腰。
glosses.en: bàn bì: halfway up the mountain.

glosses.zh: 海日：从海上升起的太阳。
glosses.en: hǎi rì: the sun rising from the sea.

glosses.zh: 天鸡：神话里的鸡。传说东南有座桃都山，山上大树上住着天鸡，太阳一照到这棵树，天鸡就叫，天下的鸡都跟着叫。
glosses.en: tiān jī: the heavenly rooster of myth. It lived in a great tree on a mountain in the southeast. When the sun first lit the tree, it crowed, and all the roosters in the world crowed after it.

glosses.zh: 千岩万转：山路在无数山岩间弯来转去。
glosses.en: qiān yán wàn zhuǎn: the path twisting among a thousand cliffs.

glosses.zh: 路不定：路的方向一直在变。
glosses.en: lù bù dìng: the way keeps changing direction.

glosses.zh: 迷花倚石：被花迷住了，靠在石头上休息。迷，迷恋。
glosses.en: mí huā yǐ shí: charmed by flowers, resting against a rock. Mí means to be enchanted.

glosses.zh: 忽已暝：不知不觉天已经黑了。暝，天色昏暗。
glosses.en: hū yǐ míng: suddenly it is already dark. Míng means dusk.

glosses.zh: 咆：怒吼。
glosses.en: páo: to roar.

glosses.zh: 吟：低沉地长鸣。
glosses.en: yín: to drone or hum long and low.

glosses.zh: 殷岩泉：声音在山岩和泉水间像雷一样轰响。殷，这里读 yǐn，形容雷声。
glosses.en: yǐn yán quán: the sound booms like thunder among the rocks and springs. Yǐn describes the rumble of thunder.

glosses.zh: 栗深林兮惊层巅：使深林战栗，使层层山峰惊动。栗，发抖；层巅，层层叠叠的山顶。
glosses.en: lì shēn lín xī jīng céng diān: making the deep woods tremble and the layered peaks shake. Lì means to tremble; céng diān means peak after peak.

glosses.zh: 兮：语气词，相当于“啊”。
glosses.en: xī: a word for rhythm, like “oh”.

glosses.zh: 青青：黑沉沉的样子。
glosses.en: qīng qīng: dark and heavy.

glosses.zh: 欲雨：快要下雨。
glosses.en: yù yǔ: about to rain.

glosses.zh: 澹澹：水波轻轻起伏的样子。
glosses.en: dàn dàn: gently rippling.

glosses.zh: 生烟：升起水汽。
glosses.en: shēng yān: giving off mist.

glosses.zh: 列缺：闪电。
glosses.en: liè quē: lightning.

glosses.zh: 霹雳：响雷。
glosses.en: pī lì: a thunderclap.

glosses.zh: 丘峦崩摧：山峰崩塌。丘峦，山丘和山峰。
glosses.en: qiū luán bēng cuī: hills and peaks crumble. Qiū luán means hills and peaks.

glosses.zh: 洞天：神仙住的洞府，洞里另有一片天地。
glosses.en: dòng tiān: a cave home of immortals, with a whole world inside.

glosses.zh: 石扉：石门。扉，门扇。
glosses.en: shí fēi: a stone door. Fēi means a door.

glosses.zh: 訇然：形容很大的声音，“轰”的一声。
glosses.en: hōng rán: with a loud boom.

glosses.zh: 中开：从中间打开。
glosses.en: zhōng kāi: opening from the middle.

glosses.zh: 青冥：青色的天空。
glosses.en: qīng míng: the blue sky.

glosses.zh: 浩荡：广阔无边的样子。
glosses.en: hào dàng: vast and endless.

glosses.zh: 金银台：金银筑成的宫阙，指神仙住的地方。
glosses.en: jīn yín tái: palaces of gold and silver, where immortals live.

glosses.zh: 霓为衣：用彩虹做衣裳。霓，彩虹的一种。
glosses.en: ní wéi yī: rainbows for clothes. Ní is a kind of rainbow.

glosses.zh: 风为马：把风当马来骑。
glosses.en: fēng wéi mǎ: the wind for horses.

glosses.zh: 云之君：云里的神仙。
glosses.en: yún zhī jūn: the lords of the clouds, gods who live in the clouds.

glosses.zh: 纷纷：一个接一个，很多的样子。
glosses.en: fēn fēn: one after another, in great numbers.

glosses.zh: 来下：降落下来。
glosses.en: lái xià: to come down.

glosses.zh: 鼓瑟：弹瑟。瑟，一种像古筝的弦乐器。
glosses.en: gǔ sè: to play the sè, a stringed instrument like a zither.

glosses.zh: 鸾：传说中像凤凰一样的神鸟。
glosses.en: luán: the luán, a magic bird like a phoenix.

glosses.zh: 回车：拉着车子回转。
glosses.en: huí chē: to turn the carriage around.

glosses.zh: 仙之人：仙人们。
glosses.en: xiān zhī rén: the immortals.

glosses.zh: 列如麻：排列得密密麻麻，像麻秆一样多。
glosses.en: liè rú má: standing in rows as thick as hemp stalks.

glosses.zh: 魂悸以魄动：心神被惊动。悸，心猛地一跳；魂魄，人的精神。
glosses.en: hún jì yǐ pò dòng: the spirit is startled. Jì means the heart jumps; hún and pò are a person's soul.

glosses.zh: 恍：猛然醒来、回过神的样子。
glosses.en: huǎng: suddenly, as one comes to oneself.

glosses.zh: 长嗟：长长地叹气。
glosses.en: cháng jiē: a long sigh.

glosses.zh: 惟：只有。
glosses.en: wéi: only.

glosses.zh: 觉时：醒来的时候。觉，睡醒，读 jué。
glosses.en: jué shí: the moment of waking. Jué means to wake up.

glosses.zh: 枕席：枕头和席子，指床铺。
glosses.en: zhěn xí: pillow and mat, that is, the bed.

glosses.zh: 向来：刚才。
glosses.en: xiàng lái: a moment ago.

glosses.zh: 烟霞：云雾和彩霞，指梦里的仙境。
glosses.en: yān xiá: mist and rosy clouds, meaning the fairyland of the dream.

glosses.zh: 行乐：寻欢作乐，享受快乐。
glosses.en: xíng lè: seeking pleasure and fun.

glosses.zh: 东流水：像向东流去的水，一去不回。
glosses.en: dōng liú shuǐ: like water flowing east, gone and never coming back.

glosses.zh: 君：你们，指东鲁的朋友。
glosses.en: jūn: you, his friends in Eastern Lu.

glosses.zh: 且：暂且。
glosses.en: qiě: for now.

glosses.zh: 白鹿：白色的鹿。传说神仙和隐士骑白鹿。
glosses.en: bái lù: a white deer. Legend says immortals and hermits rode white deer.

glosses.zh: 青崖：青山。
glosses.en: qīng yá: green cliffs.

glosses.zh: 须行即骑：要走的时候就骑上它。须，需要。
glosses.en: xū xíng jí qí: when I need to go, I will ride it. Xū means to need.

glosses.zh: 安能：怎么能。
glosses.en: ān néng: how could I.

glosses.zh: 摧眉折腰：低着眉头，弯着腰，指讨好巴结别人。
glosses.en: cuī méi zhé yāo: to lower one's brows and bend one's waist, that is, to flatter and fawn on others.

glosses.zh: 事：侍奉，伺候。
glosses.en: shì: to serve.

glosses.zh: 权贵：有权有势的人。
glosses.en: quán guì: the rich and powerful.

glosses.zh: 开心颜：心情舒畅，脸上露出笑容。
glosses.en: kāi xīn yán: a happy heart and a smiling face.

translation.zh: 航海的人谈起瀛洲，
translation.en: Seafarers talk of the island of Yingzhou,

translation.zh: 它藏在迷蒙的烟波里，实在难以找到。
translation.en: hidden in misty waves, truly hard to find.

translation.zh: 越地的人说起天姥山，
translation.en: The people of Yue talk of Mount Tianmu,

translation.zh: 在忽明忽暗的云霞里，也许能看见。
translation.en: glimpsed now and then through bright and fading clouds.

translation.zh: 天姥山高耸入云，横在天边，
translation.en: Mount Tianmu reaches the sky and stretches across it,

translation.zh: 山势超过五岳，压倒了赤城山。
translation.en: higher than the Five Great Mountains, towering over Chicheng.

translation.zh: 天台山虽然有四万八千丈高，
translation.en: Mount Tiantai, forty-eight thousand zhang tall,

translation.zh: 对着它也像要拜倒一样，向东南倾斜。
translation.en: seems to bow before it and lean away to the southeast.

translation.zh: 我根据越人的话，梦游吴越，
translation.en: Following these words, I travel in a dream to Wu and Yue,

translation.zh: 一夜之间飞过了月光下的镜湖。
translation.en: and in one night fly across Mirror Lake under the moon.

translation.zh: 湖上的月光照着我的影子，
translation.en: The moon on the lake lights up my shadow

translation.zh: 一直把我送到剡溪。
translation.en: and carries me all the way to the Shan Stream.

translation.zh: 谢灵运住过的地方如今还在，
translation.en: The place where Xie Lingyun stayed is still there,

translation.zh: 清水荡漾，猿声清亮。
translation.en: clear water rippling, apes calling in clear voices.

translation.zh: 我脚穿谢公的木屐，
translation.en: On my feet I wear Xie's wooden hiking shoes,

translation.zh: 登上高入云霄的石阶。
translation.en: and I climb stone steps into the blue clouds.

translation.zh: 到了半山腰，就看见海上升起的太阳，
translation.en: Halfway up I see the sun rise from the sea,

translation.zh: 在半空中听见天鸡的啼叫。
translation.en: and in midair I hear the heavenly rooster crow.

translation.zh: 山路在千万座山岩间回转，没有定向，
translation.en: The path winds among a thousand cliffs, never going one way;

translation.zh: 我迷恋山花，靠着山石，不知不觉天已经黑了。
translation.en: charmed by flowers, resting on rocks, I find it is suddenly dark.

translation.zh: 熊在怒吼，龙在长鸣，声音震响着山岩和泉水，
translation.en: Bears roar and dragons drone, booming through rocks and springs,

translation.zh: 让深林颤抖，让层层山峰惊动。
translation.en: making the deep woods tremble and the high peaks shake.

translation.zh: 乌云黑沉沉的，就要下雨了，
translation.en: The clouds hang dark, about to rain;

translation.zh: 水波轻轻起伏，升起了水汽。
translation.en: the water ripples softly and gives off mist.

translation.zh: 电光闪闪，雷声隆隆，
translation.en: Lightning flashes and thunder cracks,

translation.zh: 山峰都崩塌了。
translation.en: hills and peaks crumble.

translation.zh: 神仙洞府的石门，
translation.en: The stone door of the immortals' cave

translation.zh: “轰”的一声从中间打开了。
translation.en: bursts open from the middle with a boom.

translation.zh: 里面是一片青色的天空，宽广得看不到底，
translation.en: Inside, the blue sky stretches endlessly, with no bottom in sight,

translation.zh: 日月照耀着金银筑成的宫殿。
translation.en: and the sun and moon shine on palaces of gold and silver.

translation.zh: 仙人们用彩虹做衣裳，把风当马骑，
translation.en: With rainbows for clothes and the wind for horses,

translation.zh: 云中的神仙一个接一个地降落下来。
translation.en: the lords of the clouds come down one after another.

translation.zh: 老虎弹着瑟，鸾鸟拉着车，
translation.en: Tigers play the zither and phoenixes draw their carriages,

translation.zh: 仙人们排成行，密密麻麻。
translation.en: and the immortals stand in rows as thick as hemp.

translation.zh: 忽然我心惊魂动，
translation.en: Suddenly my spirit jumps in fright,

translation.zh: 猛地醒来坐起，长长叹了一口气。
translation.en: I wake with a start and let out a long sigh.

translation.zh: 醒来时只有枕头和席子，
translation.en: Waking, I find only my pillow and mat;

translation.zh: 刚才的云霞仙境全都不见了。
translation.en: the misty fairyland of a moment ago is gone.

translation.zh: 人世间的欢乐也像这梦一样，
translation.en: The pleasures of this world are just like that,

translation.zh: 自古以来，万事都像东流的水，一去不回。
translation.en: and since ancient times all things flow away like water going east.

translation.zh: 告别你们离开，什么时候才回来呢？
translation.en: I say goodbye and leave you; when will I return?

translation.zh: 暂且把白鹿放在青山之间，
translation.en: For now I will let a white deer roam among the green cliffs,

translation.zh: 要走的时候就骑上它去拜访名山。
translation.en: and when I need to go, I will ride it to visit famous mountains.

translation.zh: 我怎么能低头弯腰去伺候有权有势的人，
translation.en: How could I bow my head and bend my back to serve the powerful,

translation.zh: 让自己不能开心快乐呢！
translation.en: and never be happy at heart again!

background.zh: 天宝元年（742年），李白被唐玄宗召到长安，做了翰林供奉，就是陪在皇帝身边写文章的文人。可是他看不惯朝廷里的权贵，也受到排挤，不到三年就被“赐金放还”，也就是皇帝给些钱财，让他离开。后来他在东鲁（今山东一带）住了一段时间。一般认为天宝四载（745年）他要离开东鲁南游吴越，写下这首诗告别东鲁的朋友（一说写于天宝五载）。诗题里的“吟”是一种诗歌体裁，“留别”就是临走时留下诗来告别。
background.en: In 742, Emperor Xuanzong called Li Bai to Chang'an to serve at court, writing for the emperor. But he could not stand the powerful officials, and they pushed him out. In less than three years he was sent away with a gift of gold. Afterwards he lived for a while in Eastern Lu, around today's Shandong. The poem is usually dated to 745 (another view says 746), when he was leaving Eastern Lu to travel south to Wu and Yue, and wrote it as a goodbye to his friends there. Yín in the title is a kind of song-poem, and liú bié means leaving a poem behind as a farewell.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），字太白，号青莲居士，唐代伟大的浪漫主义诗人，被称为“诗仙”。他喜欢游山玩水、求仙访道，性格骄傲，不愿意向有权势的人低头。在长安受挫后，他更加向往自由自在的生活。这首诗里的梦中仙境和最后一句“安能摧眉折腰事权贵”，正是他这种性格的写照。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762), also called Taibai, was a great Tang poet of wild imagination, known as the Immortal of Poetry. He loved wandering in the mountains and seeking immortals. He was proud and would not bow to powerful people. After his setback in Chang'an, he longed even more for a free life. The dream fairyland in this poem, and its last cry against serving the powerful, show exactly who he was.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗讲了一场奇妙的梦。开头先从传说说起：仙山瀛洲找不到，天姥山却可能看得见，而且高得让天台山都要拜倒。于是诗人在梦里出发了：月光送他飞过镜湖，他穿上谢灵运的登山鞋，一步步爬上云梯，半山腰看日出，听天鸡叫。接着天黑了，熊吼龙鸣，电闪雷鸣，山峰崩塌，一扇石门“轰”地打开，里面是金银宫殿，神仙们穿着彩虹衣服、骑着风，成群地飞下来。就在最热闹的时候，他一下子惊醒，只剩下枕头和席子。从梦里醒来，他明白了：人间的快乐也像梦一样会过去。最后他大声说出心里话：我宁愿骑着白鹿去游名山，也不愿低头弯腰去讨好权贵。整首诗像一部从安静到热闹、再突然安静下来的电影，结尾的两句骄傲又响亮。
appreciation.en: This poem tells of a wonderful dream. It begins with legends: the island of immortals cannot be found, but Mount Tianmu might be seen, and it is so high that Mount Tiantai seems to bow before it. Then the poet sets off in his dream. The moonlight carries him across Mirror Lake. He puts on Xie Lingyun's hiking shoes and climbs step by step into the clouds, watching the sunrise and hearing the heavenly rooster halfway up. Night falls. Bears roar, dragons drone, lightning flashes, thunder cracks, and the peaks crumble. A stone door bursts open, and inside are palaces of gold and silver. Immortals dressed in rainbows ride the wind and fly down in crowds. Just when it is most exciting, he wakes with a start, and only his pillow and mat are left. Waking, he understands that the joys of this world pass like a dream too. At the end he speaks his heart aloud: he would rather ride a white deer to famous mountains than bow and bend to please the powerful. The whole poem is like a film that goes from quiet to wild and then suddenly quiet again, and the last two lines ring out proud and loud.
